title: Relative-section encoding of finite stack maps and finite atlas descent data
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal X$ a category fibred in groupoids over $\mathrm{Sch}/S$, with stack and 2-fibre-product conventions [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Use finite scheme representability [def-sfb-finite-stack-scheme-tests] and etale atlases [def-sfb-dm-stack-morphism-properties]. For a scheme map $p:Z\to T$, its section presheaf on the total category of $h_T$ sends $(U,t:U\to T)$ to $\{z:U\to Z\mid pz=t\}$ and restricts by precomposition. It is finite if $p$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. A finite relative-section presheaf on $\mathcal X$ is a functor $P:\mathcal X^{op}\to\mathrm{Set}$ whose restriction along every scheme map $t:h_T\to\mathcal X$ is naturally isomorphic to such a finite section presheaf. Morphisms are all natural transformations. Its total category has objects $(x,s)$ with $s\in P(x)$ and arrows $f:(x,s)\to(y,t)$ satisfying $P(f)(t)=s$, and projects to $\mathcal X$. Natural transformations act on the section coordinate. For a scheme map $a:h_T\to\mathcal X$, let $C_a$ have the objects of the total category of $h_T$ and arrows $c\to d$ equal to arrows $a(c)\to a(d)$ in $\mathcal X$. The ordinary chart category maps into $C_a$ by $a$. A finite atlas descent datum is a functor $C_a^{op}\to\mathrm{Set}$ restricting on ordinary chart arrows to a finite section presheaf over $T$. Its vertical-isomorphism action is the overlap isomorphism (with inverse to pass from contravariant sections to covariant transport); functoriality is the cocycle on triple overlaps, and natural transformations are all compatible scheme maps. The restriction functor from finite relative-section presheaves to finite atlas descent data is precomposition with $C_a\to\mathcal X$. These are explicit constructions, asserting no descent effectiveness.
